description: Rewrite the share-count probability instruction to give concrete calibration guidance: when strong contextual signals (authorized reverse split, explicit dilution warnings, ATM programs, distress + Nasdaq non-compliance) are present, anchor probabilities much closer to 0.85–0.95 rather than hedging at 0.3–0.5; and when the question asks about a threshold that normal run-rate alone nearly reaches, default to high probability rather than moderate. [round 3, Probability estimates for share-count questions are too low / too uncertain when evidence strongly points one direction]
